legged_robot_papers_at_ccfa: CityWalker — CVPR 2025: urban point-goal navigation learned from ~2,000 h of web video. Real Unitree Go1 + Livox Mid-360, 8-14 trials per case (forward/left/right), 50-100 m targets. SR 77.3% vs ViNT-FT 57.1%, NoMaD 42.9%.

Rethinking the Embodied Gap in VLN (VLN-PE) — ICCV 2025: physically realistic VLN on IsaacSim/GRUTopia with H1/G1/Aliengo/Jetbot. 34% relative SR drop sim -> physical. Real Go2 + D455, 14 indoor episodes, CMA SR 7.14 -> 28.57 after fine-tuning.

CogNav — ICCV 2025: LLM cognitive-state ObjectNav (GPT-4v), HM3D SR 62% -> 72.5%. Real tests on a custom mobile robot and a Unitree quadruped, shown qualitatively plus a supplementary video. Trial counts are in the supplement, not the main text.

Embodied Navigation Foundation Model (NavFoM) — ICLR 2026: cross-embodiment VLN/search/tracking model, 12.7M samples. 110 real test cases in a 5x5 m space across quadruped/humanoid/drone/wheeled robots. Inference offboard on an RTX 4090; a reviewer flagged this.

CE-Nav — ICLR 2026: IL-then-RL cross-embodiment local navigation (Go2, MagicDog, Spot, H1, quadrotor in sim). Real Go2 and MagicDog on Jetson Orin NX at >10 Hz; 40 trials x 3 scenarios vs DWA (SR 0.75) and NavRL (0.51).

UrbanVerse — ICLR 2026: real-to-sim from city-tour videos. Zero-shot sim2real on Unitree Go2 and a Coco wheeled robot over 16 unseen streets (avg 24.6 m, 3 repeats). Up to 89.7% SR; 337 m mission with 2 interventions.
Empowering Multi-Robot Cooperation via Sequential World Models (SeqWM) — ICLR 2026: Multi-Quadruped sim benchmark plus physical deployment on two Unitree Go2-W robots.

OneOcc — CVPR 2026: vision-only panoramic semantic occupancy for legged robots with Gait Displacement Compensation. Releases QuadOcc (real quadruped, 360°, 10 campus scenes, 24K frames, day/dusk/night). It is the only swept CCF-A title naming legged robots.

Let Humanoids Hike! (LEGO-H) — CVPR 2025; Gallant — CVPR 2026: humanoid (Unitree H1/G1) vision-based hiking and LiDAR-voxel locomotion/local navigation. Humanoids appear in CCF-A titles about 40x more often than quadrupeds.

Related but not CCF-A (2026 list): NaVILA — RSS 2025 (Go2 + Booster T1, 25 instructions x 3 repeats, 88% SR; R2R-CE SR 54.0). GVNav — ICRA 2025 (CCF-B), low-height quadruped VLN-CE with real quadruped.

Rejected example: L4Dog (quadruped BEV perception dataset) — ICLR 2026 submission, ratings 6/4/8, absent from proceedings. Reviewers: planar terrain only (no hills, stairs, slopes, elevators); perception-only, no VLN/VQA.

Base rate: across CVPR25, ICCV25, CVPR26, ICLR25/26, ICML25/26, NeurIPS25/26, IJCAI25 (~44.8k titles), legged platforms show up as testbeds inside nav/benchmark papers, not as title topics. AAAI and ACM MM were not swept (bot-blocked).
low_compute_success_stories: UniGoal — CVPR 2025: training-free universal goal navigation via LLM graph matching with local LLaMA-2-7B + LLaVA-v1.6-Mistral-7B in Habitat. No training at all. Both 7B models on one 8 GB GPU would need 4-bit weights (inference only).
ImagineNav — ICLR 2025: mapless VLM navigation. Only training is a ResNet-18 Where2Imagine module trained from scratch; the planner is the GPT-4o-mini API, chosen for low cost and latency.

EvoNav (History to Future) — CVPR 2026: zero-shot VLN-CE with F-CoT + H-CoE. One RTX 3090 plus Gemini-2.5-pro API. 2.4 GB inference GPU memory vs 12.5 GB for Open-Nav. Open Llama4-Maverick is comparable to GPT-4o. Real wheeled-robot test.
CogNav — ICCV 2025: training-free GPT-4v cognitive-state ObjectNav. +10.5 SR on HM3D, demonstrated on a real Unitree quadruped.

EfficientNav — NeurIPS 2025: on-device zero-shot ObjNav with small open LLMs. +11.1% SR on HM3D over GPT-4 baselines, 6.7x lower real-time latency. LLaVA-7b/LLaMA3.2-11b on one RTX A6000 and LLaVA-7b on a Jetson AGX Orin.
VLN-PE — ICCV 2025: the platform and analysis carried the paper. Baselines (CMA/Seq2Seq, ~36M params) train on one RTX 4090 in ~1 day. Real validation was only 14 Go2 episodes.
CE-Nav — ICLR 2026: every experiment on a single RTX 4090 desktop. No real robot training data (classical-planner data + RL refiner). Deployed on Go2/MagicDog at >10 Hz on Jetson Orin NX.
EMOS — ICLR 2025: LLM multi-agent framework using the GPT-4o API plus a new sim benchmark (Habitat-MAS). No model training, no real robot.

Benchmark-only accepts with no new training: CapNav — CVPR 2026 (45 real scenes, 473 tasks, 13 VLMs); NavBench — NeurIPS 2025 (3,200 QA + 432 episodes, real-robot pipeline); CitySeeker — ICLR 2026 (6,440 trajectories; best VLM 21.1%).

Training-free acceleration accepts: EfficientVLA and VLA-Cache — NeurIPS 2025 (manipulation VLAs). Zero-shot nav with no training: BeliefMapNav — NeurIPS 2025, TrajRAG and MSGNav — CVPR 2026 (compute not stated in abstracts).

Contrast (not 8 GB-feasible): NavFoM 4,032 H100-h; CityWalker 2x H100 30 h; MTU3D ~164 A100-h. NaVILA-8B inference is 18.5 GB FP16 and 8.6 GB at AWQ W4A16, so even quantized it slightly exceeds an 8 GB card.
reviewer_expectations: Data source: public HF scrape (davidheineman/iclr-2026) of 19,629 ICLR 2026 OpenReview submissions. Embodied/robot subset: 799 submissions (676 non-withdrawn), 3,096 reviews. Acceptance comes from title-matching the ICLR 2026 proceedings, so counts are lower bounds. OpenReview itself was bot-blocked.

Baselines are the most common complaint. 'Baseline/comparison' appears in 53.9% of embodied reviews; in weakness text it is 33.9% for rejected vs 26.7% for accepted papers. CAPNAV (rejected): 'compared against only one baseline, VLMaps. This is a critical flaw.'

Novelty is the clearest accept/reject separator: 21.1% of rejected vs 13.2% of accepted weakness sections. Zero-shot nav rejections cite overlap with SG-Nav/UniGoal/WMNav (HGWM) and a hand-tuned 'strategy stack' (DP-Nav). An insight is needed, not module assembly.

Training-free claims get audited. SE-VLN reviewers: 'Unfair Comparisons' from relying on proprietary APIs, an 'omniscient oracle' (ground truth used in reflection), possible data leakage from the experience repository, and missing compute/cost discussion.

Benchmark breadth: single-scene or single-dataset evaluation is penalized (CAPNAV: one MP3D scene; SE-VLN: 'confined to indoor Matterport3D'). Accepted nav papers report several standard suites (R2R-CE, RxR-CE, HM3D, MP3D, HM3D-OVON, GOAT-Bench).

Real-world validation is requested often but does not decide acceptance alone: it appears in 25.4% of weakness sections for both accepted and rejected papers. Qualitative-only demos are criticized (JanusVLN: 'only qualitative results'; HELIOS: Spot runs 'lack side-by-side performance metrics').

Typical real-world scale in accepted CCF-A papers: VLN-PE 14 episodes; CityWalker 8-14 trials x 3 cases; NaVILA (RSS) 25 instructions x 3; CE-Nav 40 trials x 3 scenarios; UrbanVerse 16 routes x 3; NavFoM 110 cases. The norm is a success-rate table vs 1-3 baselines.

Deployability and latency: NavFoM reviewer flagged real-world 'remote inference using an RTX-4090 GPU ... too large ... on-board'; OmniNav reviewer: slow-module latency 'not quantitatively analyzed'. Latency/compute terms appear in 21.7% of embodied reviews.

Statistics: trials/seeds/variance is raised in 9.7% of embodied reviews (10.8% rejected vs 9.2% accepted). The NeurIPS checklist (mandatory, desk-reject if missing) requires error bars with their meaning, plus compute type, memory and total compute.
Ablations isolating each module are expected (raised in ~20% of reviews). HGWM reviewer: most gain came from 'adding any memory', so the cost/benefit of the novel module was unclear.

Failure analysis is rarely demanded (5.9% of reviews) but strong accepted papers include it: UrbanVerse has an appendix on failure cases; VLN-PE quantifies that NaVid spins near the goal for over 25 steps in 70% of episodes.
Legged datasets: reviewers expect terrain diversity that matches legged advantages (stairs, slopes, hills, elevators) and an embodied task beyond perception (VLN/VQA). Both were L4Dog criticisms.

Base rates (ICLR 2026, lower bound): overall acceptance 28.4%, embodied/robot 35.5%, navigation 44.2%. Mean review 5.62 accepted vs 4.05 rejected. Acceptance is 38.6% when the abstract claims real-world deployment vs 34.9% otherwise.
Videos and project pages are de facto standard: video/demo terms appear in 31.4% of embodied reviews. CogNav cites its supplementary video; most accepted nav papers link project pages.
whitespace: Real egocentric legged data for embodied reasoning (not just perception). At CCF-A only OneOcc/QuadOcc exists (10 campus scenes, occupancy only). L4Dog was rejected for planar-only terrain and no VLN/VQA. A modest quadruped-height dataset with stairs/slopes plus nav/QA tasks targets a named gap.

Legged sim-to-real predictivity. VLN-PE's real validation is 14 Go2 episodes; EmbodiedSplat's sim-vs-real correlation (0.87-0.97) is wheeled Stretch only. A cheap paired sim/real protocol for a quadruped (phone-captured 3DGS of your lab, N matched episodes) is unclaimed.

Viewpoint- and gait-aware training-free agents. VLN-PE: low camera height collapses quadruped zero-shot CMA SR to 4.73. OneOcc shows gait jitter matters for perception. Zero-shot LLM/VLM agents (UniGoal, TrajRAG, MSGNav) assume Stretch/Habitat views. Explicit low-view and jitter handling is open.

Capability-conditioned closed loop. CapNav shows VLM navigation degrades as mobility constraints tighten, but tests no robot. A quadruped that can actually climb stairs/curbs is the natural platform for closing traversability reasoning -> execution.

Memory-bounded onboard agents. NavFoM and NaVILA run offboard (RTX 4090; NaVILA 8.6 GB even at W4A16); EfficientNav targets a 32 GB Jetson. Sub-8 GB VLN/ObjectNav with measured latency on legged hardware matches both reviewer asks and your hardware.

Stop and terminal-decision reliability. VLN-PE reports unreliable stopping on the real Go2 (stop threshold 1e-4) and NaVid goal-spinning in 70% of episodes. A failure taxonomy plus a lightweight fix (verifier or uncertainty-gated stop) on a real quadruped is under-served (inferred from swept papers).

Fair open-model evaluation. Reviewers penalize API-only comparisons (SE-VLN). EvoNav shows an open model can match GPT-4o. Running everything with small local VLMs and reporting cost/latency is cheap for you and pre-empts a known critique.

Legged real-to-sim eval sets. 3DGS nav benchmarks (SAGE-3D/InteriorGS, NavBench-GS, EmbodiedSplat) use wheeled or abstract agents. A small legged-view 3DGS eval set with measured sim-real correlation was not found among swept titles (inference, not exhaustive).
venue_notes: CCF 2026 list (PDF dated 2026-04-09, hosted by HDU; text extracted locally). AI conference class A: AAAI, NeurIPS, ACL, CVPR, ICCV, ICML, ICLR. Graphics/Multimedia class A: ACM MM, SIGGRAPH, VR, IEEE VIS. AI journal class A: AI, TPAMI, IJCV, JMLR.

IJCAI is class B in the 2026 list, alongside ECCV, ICRA and AAMAS. IROS is class C, T-RO is class B, and CoRL/RSS are not listed. Any future IJCAI paper therefore no longer counts as CCF-A under the 2026 list.
Venue fit from counts: zero-shot/training-free nav titles cluster at CVPR/ICCV/NeurIPS (10 of 10), with none at ICLR/ICML 2025-26. ICLR rewards trained foundation models with real-robot breadth.

Embodied-nav accepted titles per venue: CVPR25 8, ICCV25 15, CVPR26 28, ICLR25 4, ICLR26 17, ICML25 3, ICML26 11, NeurIPS25 13, NeurIPS26 20; IJCAI25 had only a survey. The trend is rising, with CVPR26 the largest.
method_caveats: Counts come from official listings (openaccess.thecvf.com, proceedings.iclr.cc, proceedings.neurips.cc, proceedings.mlr.press v267, ijcai.org, icml.cc/neurips.cc virtual 2026) using title-keyword matching. These are lower bounds: many legged papers do not say 'quadruped' in the title.
Not swept: AAAI 2025/2026 (ojs.aaai.org), ACM MM 2025 (dl.acm.org) and DBLP were all bot-check blocked. CVPR 2026 and NeurIPS/ICML 2026 counts are from public listings as of 2026-10-19.
Review statistics come from a third-party HF scrape of OpenReview, not OpenReview directly. Keyword percentages are rough signals: 'video' and 'real-world' also match non-request mentions.

The web-search budget ran out partway through. Later facts come from direct fetches of known primary URLs (PDFs/abstract pages), not new searches. ICML 2025 MASQ/A2Perf (found via icml.cc search hits) were not in the PMLR v267 title list, so they are excluded.
Two different CVPR 2025 papers are titled 'Vid2Sim'. Only the urban-navigation one is cited here as an example; no compute figure is attached to it.
